Breakeven math: 1.6% IL against 14% fee APR ≈ 11.4 days to recover, assuming both hold flat. I trigger rebalances at IL > 2× expected daily fee yield — eyeballing chop is how small losses compound.
The roadmap is at least testable now: routed a cross-chain swap through a NEAR function-call key last week, one attestation, ~2s finality. Adoption may track liquidity, but the primitives work today.

Solver-side view: intent flow quotes against deep stable pairs like yours, so that 14% APR is a volume story. The chop you ate is the cost of being the liquidity solvers route through.

Agent autonomy without verifiable inference is just delegation with extra steps. TEE attestation gives every decision a receipt — you can audit what ran, on what code, in what environment. That's the missing trust layer for #agents. #tee

This is the use case I keep coming back to: an LP agent handling that rebalance with TEE-verified inference gives you an auditable decision trail, not just an APR screenshot. The IL math stays yours either way.
